result.title: Direct GPU Energy Measurements of Batch-Level Sharing in Mixture-of-Experts and Recurrent Models
result.summary: Energy claims for efficient neural networks are often inferred from operation counts. We report direct GPU energy measurements on two workloads that batch very differently, recurrent policies in GPU-vectorised multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) and mixture-of-experts (MoE) language models, and ask one question of both: can the rows of a batch be made to share computation, across the batch and over time, at a measured saving? On recurrent policies the answer so far is no. Shared activity patterns exist but rarely last one step, masking a frozen policy fails, and trained-in masks succeed only because a fixed mask is equivalent to a narrow GRU, at 11x the energy of a small dense policy in our implementation. Test-time steering adds nothing beyond re-picking on either workload. On MoE models the answer is yes, and granularity decides how much: on Qwen3-30B-A3B, batch-aware routing reads 25-31% fewer expert weights within KL 0.05, with benchmark changes within noise at 500 items, and uses 12-18% less energy per token on a fused forward. We also introduce persistence-aware OEA, a one-parameter rule that keeps the batch-aware cut with about 40% fewer new experts per step than native routing at batch 32-64, though its energy has not yet been measured. These are pilot measurements on one GPU type, and we state their limits.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在两类批次特性迥异的工作负载（GPU向量化MARL的循环策略与MoE语言模型）上直接测量GPU能耗，检验批次内及跨时间的计算共享能否带来实测节能；结果显示循环策略上共享基本失败，而MoE上batch-aware routing可在KL 0.05内减少25–31%专家权重读取、每token能耗降12–18%，并提出persistence-aware OEA规则。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「用实测GPU能耗替代操作计数」的做法，以及关于批次级共享、循环状态持久性与test-time steering无增益的分析，可供核查LVR中循环/动态计算（THINK/LOOK/STOP）的真实成本与latent状态复用价值时借鉴；但该文为非多模态、单GPU试点，迁移性仍需核查。
